- Neutral cross-examination closed every single-sourced claim: Sol independently confirmed the 3.x `passwd-tries` leftover, Opus confirmed the `#include` lexer point, and Sol corrected its own data-loss framing.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the rename fixes the ordering for the file it renames. sudo parses `@includedir` files in byte order (`strcmp`) and applies `Defaults` in parse order, so the last `passwd_tries` value wins. `10-omarchy-passwd-tries` is parsed before a user's `99-passwd-tries`, so the user's value now takes effect on installs whose only Omarchy `passwd_tries` file is the packaged one. The rename needs no packaging change: `omarchy-settings` copies `etc/` wholesale and sets sudoers drop-ins to 0440. On a normal `omarchy update`, pacman removes the old package-owned `omarchy-passwd-tries` in the same transaction, before migrations run. The new test passes on the PR head and fails against base files at the packaged-name check.

Two gaps remain: a 3.x-era drop-in that still overrides the user's value on upgraded machines, and a migration that exits before doing anything.

### Machines upgraded from 3.x keep a later-sorting `passwd-tries` file

The 3.x installer (`install/config/increase-sudo-tries.sh` at [v3.8.4](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/v3.8.4/install/config/increase-sudo-tries.sh#L1-L3)) wrote `Defaults passwd_tries=10` to `/etc/sudoers.d/passwd-tries`. A migration that removed it ([`1779303581.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/3636f57f0ccfe1b690321b21b4d337d6e57664ac/migrations/1779303581.sh#L13-L15)) was deleted when migrations were collapsed for 4.0 ([75cb4f7](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/commit/75cb4f7195cfc064d05cd30623b3254c9541ba3c)). Nothing at the PR head or the current `quattro` tip removes it, including `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`. No package owns the file, so pacman leaves it in place.

```text
sudo parse order on a 3.x -> 4.x upgraded machine, after this PR

10-omarchy-passwd-tries   passwd_tries=10   (package)
99-passwd-tries           passwd_tries=3    (user override from #12397)
passwd-tries              passwd_tries=10   (3.x installer)  <- parsed last, wins
```

**Impact:** the #12397 override still has no effect on machines upgraded from 3.x. Fresh 4.x installs are not affected. This gap predates the PR, but it limits what the fix achieves for upgraded machines. Whether the reporter's machine is a 3.x upgrade is unknown.

**Suggested change:** have the migration also remove `/etc/sudoers.d/passwd-tries` when its content is exactly the 3.x installer's one-liner, and leave any other content alone. This depends on the elevated checks described in the next finding.

### The migration exits before checking the old file

`migrations/1789838300.sh:18` runs `[[ -e $old || -L $old ]] || exit 0` without elevation. `/etc/sudoers.d` is 0750 root:root, and `omarchy-migrate` runs as the logged-in user. The user cannot search that directory, so both tests are false whether or not the file exists. The script exits 0 without calling `sudo`, and `omarchy-migrate` marks it done for that user. The repository documents the same trap in `migrations/1788025225.sh` and tests for it in `test/shell.d/retired-installer-artifacts-migration-test.sh`.

A sandboxed run with a stub `sudo` confirmed this. When the calling user could not search the directory, the migration made no `sudo` call, exited 0 and left a stock old file in place. The PR test still passes, because it only checks that the migration contains two strings.

**Impact:** low for the package-owned `omarchy-passwd-tries`, because pacman already removes it. The cleanup described in the PR never happens, though, and an unowned leftover copy would stay. Because completion markers are per filename, a later fix needs a new migration file. The migration's "leave custom contents alone" guard also cannot apply to the package-owned file: pacman removes that file before migrations run, and `omarchy-settings` does not list it in `backup=()`, so pacman already overwrote local edits to it on earlier upgrades.

**Suggested change:** either drop the migration and state that pacman removes the old path, or make the checks elevated as `migrations/1788025225.sh` does:
- Probe for the file and read it through `sudo`. Exit non-zero when that fails, instead of `2>/dev/null || true`, so the migration stays pending.
- Compare the whole file with the exact stock line (`[[ $body == 'Defaults passwd_tries=10' ]]`) instead of stripping lines that start with `#`. sudo treats `#include` and `#includedir` at the start of a line as active directives, not comments. The current stripping would classify a file containing either one as stock and delete it once the check runs elevated.
- Cover this with the stub-`sudo` pattern from `retired-installer-artifacts-migration-test.sh`: an unsearchable directory, the stock file, the stock file plus `#include`, and a failing `sudo`.
